texts: Hemoconcentration is not a risk factor for neurologic injury: D.

After bypass, ultrafiltration concentrates the diluted blood and raises the haematocrit; in infants, a low haematocrit on bypass has been linked to worse neurodevelopment, so concentrating the blood is protective rather than harmful.
Deep hypothermic circulatory arrest, especially when long, blood transfusion, reperfusion injury and anaesthetic agents are listed among the risks to the developing brain.
In the picture, only the strainer that thickens the river leaves the head lantern glowing calm.
Memory hook: a thicker red river keeps the lantern calm.
